items.text:
श्रुत्वा धर्मं विजानाति श्रुत्वा त्यजति दुर्मतिम् ।
श्रुत्वा ज्ञानमवाप्नोति श्रुत्वा मोक्षमवाप्नुयात् ॥१॥
items.tr:
śrutvā dharmaṃ vijānāti śrutvā tyajati durmatim |
śrutvā jñānamavāpnoti śrutvā mokṣamavāpnuyāt ||1||
items.en: By listening one learns what is right, by listening one gives up bad thinking, by listening one gains knowledge, and by listening one may reach freedom.

items.text:
पक्षिणां काकचाण्डालः पशूनां चैव कुक्कुरः ।
मुनीनां पापी चाण्डालः सर्वचाण्डालनिन्दकः ॥२॥
items.tr:
pakṣiṇāṃ kākacāṇḍālaḥ paśūnāṃ caiva kukkuraḥ |
munīnāṃ pāpī cāṇḍālaḥ sarvacāṇḍālanindakaḥ ||2||
items.en: Among birds the crow is the lowest, among animals the dog, among holy men the sinner; but the one who speaks ill of others is the lowest of all.

items.text:
भस्मना शुध्यते कांस्यं ताम्रमम्लेन शुध्यति ।
रजसा शुध्यते नारि नदी वेगेन शुध्यति ॥३॥
items.tr:
bhasmanā śudhyate kāṃsyaṃ tāmramamlena śudhyati |
rajasā śudhyate nāri nadī vegena śudhyati ||3||
items.en: Bronze is cleaned by ash, copper by something sour, a woman by her monthly course, and a river by its flow.

items.text:
भ्रमन्संपूज्यते राजा भ्रमन्संपूज्यते द्विजः ।
भ्रमन्संपूज्यते योगी स्त्री भ्रमन्ती विनश्यति ॥४॥
items.tr:
bhramansaṃpūjyate rājā bhramansaṃpūjyate dvijaḥ |
bhramansaṃpūjyate yogī strī bhramantī vinaśyati ||4||
items.en: A king who travels is honoured, a Brahmin who travels is honoured, a yogi who travels is honoured, but a woman who wanders is ruined.

items.text:
यस्यार्थास्तस्य मित्राणि यस्यर्थास्तस्य बांधवाः ।
यस्याथाः स पुमांल्लोके यस्यार्थाः सच पण्डितः ॥५॥
items.tr:
yasyārthāstasya mitrāṇi yasyarthāstasya bāṃdhavāḥ |
yasyāthāḥ sa pumāṃlloke yasyārthāḥ saca paṇḍitaḥ ||5||
items.en: One who has money has friends and relatives; he is counted a man in the world, and he is even called learned.

items.text:
तादृशी जायते बुध्दिर्व्यवसायोऽपि तादृशः ।
सहायास्तादृशा एव यादृशी भवितव्यता ॥६॥
items.tr:
tādṛśī jāyate budhdirvyavasāyo'pi tādṛśaḥ |
sahāyāstādṛśā eva yādṛśī bhavitavyatā ||6||
items.en: As fate is going to be, so the mind turns, so the effort becomes, and so the helpers appear.

items.text:
कालः पचति भूतानि कालः संहरते प्रजाः ।
कालः सुप्तेषु जागर्ति कालो हि दुरतिक्रमः ॥७॥
items.tr:
kālaḥ pacati bhūtāni kālaḥ saṃharate prajāḥ |
kālaḥ supteṣu jāgarti kālo hi duratikramaḥ ||7||
items.en: Time ripens all beings and time destroys them; time is awake while others sleep; truly, time is hard to escape.

items.text:
नैव पश्यति जन्माधः कामान्धो नैव पश्यति ।
मदोन्मत्ता न पश्यन्ति अर्थी दोषं न पश्यति ॥८॥
items.tr:
naiva paśyati janmādhaḥ kāmāndho naiva paśyati |
madonmattā na paśyanti arthī doṣaṃ na paśyati ||8||
items.en: One born blind cannot see, one blinded by lust cannot see, those drunk with pride cannot see, and one who wants something sees no fault in it.

items.text:
स्वयं कर्म करोत्यत्मा स्वयं तत्फलमश्नुते ।
स्वयं भ्रमति संसारे स्वयं तस्माद्विमुच्यते ॥९॥
items.tr:
svayaṃ karma karotyatmā svayaṃ tatphalamaśnute |
svayaṃ bhramati saṃsāre svayaṃ tasmādvimucyate ||9||
items.en: The soul does its own deeds and enjoys their fruit itself; it wanders through the world by itself and frees itself by itself.

items.text:
राजा राष्ट्रकृतं पापं राज्ञः पापं पुरोहितः ।
भर्ता च स्त्रीकृतं पापं शिष्यपापं गुरुस्तथा ॥१०॥
items.tr:
rājā rāṣṭrakṛtaṃ pāpaṃ rājñaḥ pāpaṃ purohitaḥ |
bhartā ca strīkṛtaṃ pāpaṃ śiṣyapāpaṃ gurustathā ||10||
items.en: The king bears the sins of his country, the priest the sins of the king, the husband the sins of his wife, and the teacher the sins of his pupil.

items.text:
ऋणकर्ता पिता शत्रुमाता च व्यभिचारिणी ।
भार्या रूपवती शत्रुः पुत्रः शत्रुरपण्डितः ॥११॥
items.tr:
ṛṇakartā pitā śatrumātā ca vyabhicāriṇī |
bhāryā rūpavatī śatruḥ putraḥ śatrurapaṇḍitaḥ ||11||
items.en: A father in debt is an enemy, so is an unfaithful mother, a beautiful wife, and a son without learning.

items.text:
लुब्धमर्थेन गृहिणीयात् स्तब्धमञ्जलिकर्मणा ।
मूर्खं छन्दानुवृत्या च यथार्थत्वेन पण्डितम् ॥१२॥
items.tr:
lubdhamarthena gṛhiṇīyāt stabdhamañjalikarmaṇā |
mūrkhaṃ chandānuvṛtyā ca yathārthatvena paṇḍitam ||12||
items.en: Win a greedy person with money, a proud one with folded hands, a fool by going along with him, and a wise one with the truth.

items.text:
वरं न राज्यं न कुराजराज्यं
वरं न मित्रं न कुमित्रमित्रम् ।
वरं न शिष्यो न कुशिष्यशिष्यो
वरं न दारा न कुदारदाराः ॥१३॥
items.tr:
varaṃ na rājyaṃ na kurājarājyaṃ
varaṃ na mitraṃ na kumitramitram |
varaṃ na śiṣyo na kuśiṣyaśiṣyo
varaṃ na dārā na kudāradārāḥ ||13||
items.en: Better no kingdom than a kingdom under a bad king; better no friend than a bad friend; better no pupil than a bad pupil; better no wife than a bad wife.

items.text:
कुराजराज्येन कुतः प्रजासुखं
कुमित्रमित्रेण कुतोऽभिनिर्वृतिः ।
कुदारदारैश्च कुतो गृहे रतिः
कुशिष्यमध्यापयतः कुतो यशः ॥१४॥
items.tr:
kurājarājyena kutaḥ prajāsukhaṃ
kumitramitreṇa kuto'bhinirvṛtiḥ |
kudāradāraiśca kuto gṛhe ratiḥ
kuśiṣyamadhyāpayataḥ kuto yaśaḥ ||14||
items.en: How can people be happy under a bad king? What comfort comes from a bad friend? What joy is there at home with a bad wife? What fame comes from teaching a bad pupil?

items.text:
सिंहादेकं वकादेकं शिक्षेच्चत्वारि कुक्कुटात् ।
वायसात्पञ्च शिक्षेच्चष्ट् शुनस्त्रीणिगर्दभात् ॥१५॥
items.tr:
siṃhādekaṃ vakādekaṃ śikṣeccatvāri kukkuṭāt |
vāyasātpañca śikṣeccaṣṭ śunastrīṇigardabhāt ||15||
items.en: Learn one thing from the lion, one from the crane, four from the rooster, five from the crow, six from the dog, and three from the donkey.

items.text:
प्रभूतं कार्यमपि वा तन्नरः कर्तुमिच्छति ।
सर्वारम्भेण तत्कार्यं सिंहादेकं प्रचक्षते ॥१६॥
items.tr:
prabhūtaṃ kāryamapi vā tannaraḥ kartumicchati |
sarvārambheṇa tatkāryaṃ siṃhādekaṃ pracakṣate ||16||
items.en: Whatever task a person wants to do, great or small, he should do it with full effort; this one thing is learned from the lion.

items.text:
इन्द्रियाणि च संयम्य वकवत् पण्डितो नरः ।
देशकालबलं ज्ञात्वा सर्वकार्याणि साधयेत् ॥१७॥
items.tr:
indriyāṇi ca saṃyamya vakavat paṇḍito naraḥ |
deśakālabalaṃ jñātvā sarvakāryāṇi sādhayet ||17||
items.en: A wise person should control his senses like a crane and, knowing the place, the time and his own strength, carry out all his tasks.

items.text:
प्रत्युत्थानञ्च युध्द्ञ्च संविभागञ्च बन्धुषु ।
स्वयमाक्रम्यभुक्तञ्चशिक्षेच्चत्वारिकुक्कुटात् ॥१८॥
items.tr:
pratyutthānañca yudhdñca saṃvibhāgañca bandhuṣu |
svayamākramyabhuktañcaśikṣeccatvārikukkuṭāt ||18||
items.en: Waking early, being ready to fight, sharing with his kin, and winning his own food by effort: learn these four from the rooster.

items.text:
गूढमैथुनचारित्वं काले काले च संग्रहम् ।
अप्रमत्तमविश्वासं पञ्च शिक्षेच्च वायसात् ॥१९॥
items.tr:
gūḍhamaithunacāritvaṃ kāle kāle ca saṃgraham |
apramattamaviśvāsaṃ pañca śikṣecca vāyasāt ||19||
items.en: Mating in private, storing things from time to time, staying alert, and not trusting easily: learn these five from the crow.

items.text:
बह्वाशी स्वल्पसन्तुष्टः सनिद्रो लघुचेतनः ।
स्वामिभक्तश्च शूरश्च षडेतो श्वानतोगुणाः ॥२०॥
items.tr:
bahvāśī svalpasantuṣṭaḥ sanidro laghucetanaḥ |
svāmibhaktaśca śūraśca ṣaḍeto śvānatoguṇāḥ ||20||
items.en: Eating much but being content with little, sleeping deeply yet waking easily, loyalty to the master, and courage: these six are the dog's qualities.

items.text:
सुश्रान्तोऽपि वहेत भारं शीतोष्णं न च पश्यति ।
सन्तुष्टश्चरते नित्यं त्रीणि शिक्षेच्च गर्दभात् ॥२१॥
items.tr:
suśrānto'pi vaheta bhāraṃ śītoṣṇaṃ na ca paśyati |
santuṣṭaścarate nityaṃ trīṇi śikṣecca gardabhāt ||21||
items.en: Carrying a load even when very tired, not minding cold or heat, and always going about content: learn these three from the donkey.

items.text:
एतान् विंशतिगुणानाचरिष्यति मानवः ।
कार्यावस्थासु सर्वासु अजेयः स भविष्यति ॥२२॥
items.tr:
etān viṃśatiguṇānācariṣyati mānavaḥ |
kāryāvasthāsu sarvāsu ajeyaḥ sa bhaviṣyati ||22||
items.en: A person who practises these twenty qualities will be unbeatable in every kind of work.
